hard_dependencies.name: native fixture adapter interfaces
hard_dependencies.reason: The bootstrap, object_event/script macros, map-header boundaries, spawn loader and named symbols in observer.hpp, profile_native.hpp and the existing smoke frontend form the explicit engine adapter. Their names and semantics must exist; all resolved addresses and record constants are derived. The generated adapter-bindings.json lists each current symbolic binding.

hard_dependencies.name: native avatar palette mapping assertions
hard_dependencies.reason: The source adapter reads the four PLAYER_* + 1 == PAL_NPC_* declarations in SpawnPlayer. This chooses stress colors distinct from the current avatars, without fixing selector IDs, names or RGB values. A change to this mapping codec requires adapting one parser.

hard_dependencies.name: DAY and MORN
hard_dependencies.reason: Palette selection enumerates the current time-of-day declaration; the native software clock and real palette engine produce daytime/night references.

hard_dependencies.name: itemball_event and POTION
hard_dependencies.reason: Produce ordinary item balls through the real macro, with a harmless current native item identity. This exercises the real object priority class instead of an NPC with item graphics.

hard_dependencies.name: IN_DARKNESS, PALETTE_AUTO and PALETTE_NITE
hard_dependencies.reason: Exercise real local time-of-day and darkness branches through a temporary native map header. Their numeric bits and all color outputs are derived.

hard_dependencies.name: native map/collision source codec
hard_dependencies.reason: The source adapter reads named MapScriptHeader tables, one block index per .ablk byte, square row-major collision entries and the FLOOR collision identity. This avoids creating maps or choosing immutable coordinates. Changing this source codec requires updating the single parser; block width and map dimensions are derived.

hard_dependencies.name: wGameTimerPaused, wGameTimeCap and wGameTimeFrames
hard_dependencies.reason: Exact save tests choose fixed elapsed-time/software-RTC input. These clock fields are initialized before joining; normal world frames, audio, interrupts and network stay live. Performance/rendering cases use normal native clocks.

derived_inputs.derivation: Derive the current avatar palette roles from SpawnPlayer and select seven distinct day color values outside that set; record selectors and encoded colors in the fixture manifest. No named color is mandatory. The actual native renders must confirm all eleven requested colors are distinct.

derived_inputs.name: battery capacity and initial unused bytes
derived_inputs.derivation: Create and retain a fresh erased battery image of exactly the current capacity, identically for both controls. No save format, record layout or historic battery file is assumed.

derived_inputs.name: receiver-specific ordinary activation
derived_inputs.source: current native map/object loader and native figure-demand observer
derived_inputs.derivation: The primary crowded receiver must establish twelve ordinary objects. Native eligibility is read from each frame of the singleplayer control and matched by original map-object identity. Workload avatar doubles are excluded; hiding multiplayer demand cannot waive a native-visible figure.

derived_inputs.name: shared current native initialization data
derived_inputs.source: fresh native seed producer and current ordinary save/load routines
derived_inputs.derivation: The current singleplayer ROM produces a settled native save for each avatar. Both counterparts load that exact fresh file, then construct the requested map objects through the native loader. Daily NPC/phone/RNG values and string padding are carried as native-generated data, without dependencies on their individual fields or results.

acceptance_limits_reason: Explicit acceptance ceilings, not fitted to the current renderer. Existing native omissions and world-update gaps are retained in paired controls. No CPU-heavy frame is silently removed from presentation coverage.
hardware_contracts: Forty OAM entries and ten selected sprites per scanline
core_interface: The enabled ROM uses MBC30 and libmobile. Use the project's pinned read-only observer, with MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CORE and MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CORE_SOURCE overrides for equivalent supported platforms. Emulator state recovery requires compatible serialization, not cross-core state conversion.
coverage_boundary: Finite scenarios and deterministic generated byte/event sequences do not prove safety for every possible machine state. Manual footprint judgement remains required. Synthetic scene tests and unchanged-release tests are reported separately.
